title: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant G

parts.title: Part 1.1
parts.instructions: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant G | Part 1.1 - level A1-A2 - 3 questions (scored items 1-3). The examiner asks you three short questions about yourself and your interests, one after another. There is NO preparation time. You have 30 seconds to answer each question. Begin speaking when you hear the chime. Part one continues with the two photographs of Part 1.2.

questions.q:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant G | Part 1.1 (A1-A2) - items 1-3

STAGE DIRECTION: Greet the candidate, check the name on the register, and confirm the recording has started. Read the opening exactly as written. Ask the three questions one after another. Do NOT give preparation time. Allow 30 seconds for each answer; stop the candidate politely at 30 seconds and move straight on. Part one is not finished after these three questions - the two photographs of Part 1.2 belong to the same part.

EXAMINER: Good morning. Before we begin, could you tell me your full name, please?
EXAMINER: Thank you. This is the Speaking test, Variant G. It has four parts.

EXAMINER (read exactly): "Part one. In this part, I am going to ask you three short questions about yourself and your interests. And then, you will see some photos and answer some questions about them. You will have 30 seconds to reply to each question. Begin speaking when you hear this sound (chime)."

QUESTION 1 (30 seconds) - (chime)
EXAMINER: What kind of music do you like listening to?
[Allow 30 seconds. At 30 seconds say: "Thank you."]

QUESTION 2 (30 seconds) - (chime)
EXAMINER: When do you usually listen to music - at home, or when you are travelling?
[Allow 30 seconds. At 30 seconds say: "Thank you."]

QUESTION 3 (30 seconds) - (chime)
EXAMINER: Have you ever learnt to play a musical instrument, or would you like to? Tell me about it.
[Allow 30 seconds. At 30 seconds say: "Thank you."]

EXAMINER: Thank you. We are still in part one. Now look at these two photographs.

EXAMINER NOTE: Questions 1-3 are scored together as items 1, 2 and 3 (0-5 in total). One or two short sentences with a simple reason are enough at this level; do not reward or penalise the candidate's taste in music, and do not ask follow-up questions of your own.

parts.title: Part 1.2
parts.instructions: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant G | Part 1.2 - level B1 - 3 questions (scored items 4-6). You will see two photographs on one theme. First you compare and describe them (45 seconds), then you answer two opinion questions (30 seconds each). There is NO preparation time. Begin speaking when you hear the chime.

questions.q:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant G | Part 1.2 (B1) - items 4-6

STAGE DIRECTION: Show the candidate the two photographs side by side (or, if no photographs are available, read the bracketed descriptions aloud, slowly, once). Ask the three questions one after another. Do NOT give preparation time. Question 4 lasts 45 seconds; questions 5 and 6 last 30 seconds each.

[PICTURE 1: a crowded open-air street market in the late morning. A woman in a headscarf is holding up a bunch of carrots while a stallholder in a green apron weighs tomatoes on old brass scales. Wooden crates of fruit are stacked behind them, prices are written by hand on pieces of cardboard, and other shoppers are pushing past with cloth bags over their shoulders.]

[PICTURE 2: the self-service checkout area of a modern supermarket late in the evening. One young man stands alone at a touchscreen machine, scanning a packet of pasta with his phone held ready to pay. The floor is polished and empty, the lighting is bright and white, and a long row of unstaffed checkouts stretches away behind him.]

EXAMINER (read exactly): "Now, I am going to ask you to compare two pictures and I will ask you two questions about them. Look at the photographs. What do you see in these pictures?"

QUESTION 4 - COMPARE AND DESCRIBE THE TWO PICTURES (45 seconds) - (chime)
[Question 4 is the question you have just read out - "What do you see in these pictures?" Do not read it a second time. Start the 45 seconds at the chime. If the candidate describes only one photograph, or stops early, prompt ONCE: "And the other picture? How are they different?" At 45 seconds say: "Thank you."]

QUESTION 5 - OPINION (30 seconds) - (chime)
EXAMINER: Which of these two places would you choose for your weekly shopping, and why?
[Allow 30 seconds. At 30 seconds say: "Thank you."]

QUESTION 6 - OPINION (30 seconds) - (chime)
EXAMINER: Some people say it is better to pay with cash than with a card or a phone. What do you think?
[Allow 30 seconds. At 30 seconds say: "Thank you."]

EXAMINER: Thank you. That is the end of part one.

EXAMINER NOTE: Questions 4-6 are scored together as items 4, 5 and 6 (0-5 in total). Reward description of both photographs plus a personal opinion that is justified; the candidate does not have to prefer either picture, and neither answer is "correct".

parts.title: Part 2
parts.instructions: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant G | Part 2 - level B2 - one picture and 3 questions presented at once (scored item 7). You are NOT required to describe the picture; it is only there to introduce the theme. You have 1 minute to think, then 2 minutes to answer all three questions together. Begin speaking when you hear the chime.

questions.q:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant G | Part 2 (B2) - item 7

STAGE DIRECTION: Show the picture and read all three questions AT ONCE, then start the preparation timer. Give 1 minute of silent preparation (the candidate may make notes), then 2 minutes to answer all three questions together. Do not interrupt during the two minutes unless the candidate falls silent for more than ten seconds; then prompt with the next question only.

EXAMINER (read exactly): "Part two. In this part, I am going to show you a picture and ask you three questions. You will have one minute to think about your answers before you start speaking. You will have two minutes to answer all three questions. Begin speaking when you hear this sound (chime). Look at the photograph."

[PICTURE: a teenage girl sitting cross-legged on her bedroom floor, counting banknotes and coins that are spread out over an open exercise book. A hand-written savings plan with ticks down one side is taped to the wardrobe door behind her, and a catalogue of bicycles lies open beside her knee.]

EXAMINER: You do not have to describe the picture. Here are your three questions.

QUESTION 7a: Tell me about something you saved money for over a long time.
QUESTION 7b: How has saving for it changed the way you spend money now?
QUESTION 7c: In general, what do you think has the strongest influence on how people decide to spend or save - their family, their income, or advertising?

EXAMINER: You now have one minute to think. [Start the timer. Remain silent for 60 seconds.]
EXAMINER: Your minute is up. You have two minutes to answer all three questions. (chime)
[Time 2 minutes. At 1 minute 45 seconds, if the candidate has not reached the third question, say quietly: "And the last question, please." At 2 minutes say: "Thank you. That is the end of part two."]

EXAMINER NOTE: Part 2 is scored as item 7 (0-5). The picture only evokes the theme; a candidate who never mentions the picture is not penalised. Reward movement from personal experience to a general, reasoned position, with advantages and drawbacks weighed up.

parts.title: Part 3
parts.instructions:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant G | Part 3 - level C1 - ONE question (scored item 8). You will see a topic statement and two lists of points, FOR and AGAINST, with three points in each. Choose two points from each list and give a balanced argument representing both sides. You have 1 minute to prepare and 2 minutes to speak.

EXAMINER NOTE - SCORING OF THE WHOLE SPEAKING PAPER:
 - Items 1-3 (Part 1.1, the three personal questions) are scored together: 0-5.
 - Items 4-6 (Part 1.2, the two pictures and the two opinion questions) are scored together: 0-5.
 - Item 7 (Part 2) is scored: 0-5.
 - Item 8 (Part 3) is scored: 0-6.
 - Maximum raw score: 21. The raw score is then converted to a rating out of 75.

OFFICIAL RAW SCORE -> RATING CONVERSION TABLE:
21=75, 20.5=73, 20=71, 19.5=69, 19=67, 18.5=65, 18=64, 17.5=63, 17=61, 16.5=59, 16=57, 15.5=56, 15=54, 14.5=52, 14=51, 13.5=50, 13=49, 12.5=47, 12=46, 11.5=45, 11=43, 10.5=42, 10=40, 9.5=39, 9=38, 8.5=37, 8=35, 7.5=33, 7=32, 6.5=30, 6=29, 5.5=27, 5=26, 4.5=24, 4=23, 3.5=21, 3=19, 2.5=17, 2=15, 1.5=13, 1=11, 0.5=10, 0=0

questions.q:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant G | Part 3 (C1) - item 8

STAGE DIRECTION: Show the topic statement and the two lists together, or read them aloud once, slowly. Give 1 minute of silent preparation, then 2 minutes to speak. The candidate must choose TWO points from the FOR list and TWO points from the AGAINST list and build one balanced argument covering both sides.

EXAMINER (read exactly): "Part three. In this part, you are going to speak on a topic for two minutes. You can see the topic on the screen and two lists of points - for and against - related to the topic. Choose two items from each list and give a balanced argument to represent both sides of the topic. You have one minute to prepare your argument. You will then have two minutes to speak. Begin speaking when you hear this sound (chime)."

TOPIC STATEMENT:
"Shops should be required by law to print the environmental cost of a product next to its price."

FOR
 1. Shoppers cannot make responsible choices while the real cost of a product is hidden from them.
 2. Informed customers put commercial pressure on producers to clean up how goods are made and transported.
 3. A figure printed on the shelf makes it far harder to pretend that a very cheap product costs nothing to produce.

AGAINST
 1. Such a cost cannot be calculated fairly, and whoever sets the method can quietly make their own goods look better.
 2. The expense of measuring and printing it is passed on in the price, and it is the poorest shoppers who feel that first.
 3. Most people already ignore the information on labels, so one more number is unlikely to change what ends up in the basket.

EXAMINER: Choose two points from each list. You have one minute to prepare. [Start the timer. Remain silent for 60 seconds.]
EXAMINER: Your minute is up. You have two minutes to speak. (chime)
[Time 2 minutes. If the candidate presents only one side by 1 minute 15 seconds, prompt once: "And the other side of the argument, please." At 2 minutes say: "Thank you. That is the end of the Speaking test."]

EXAMINER NOTE: Part 3 is scored as item 8 (0-6). A candidate who argues only one side, however well, cannot reach the top bands. The candidate is not required to state a personal verdict at the end, but a reasoned conclusion is credited.
